title: Chicago Tavern-Style Pizza Dough

items.body: Put the flour, sugar, salt and yeast in the mixer bowl and whisk to combine.
Add the water and oil. Mix on low with the dough hook, scraping down the bowl now and then, until it comes together in a shaggy ball. Cover the bowl and rest 10 min.
Knead on medium-low until silky and pulling away from the sides of the bowl, ≈5 min.
Turn out onto a lightly floured counter and cut into 2 pieces of ≈250 g. Shape each into a smooth ball, coat it lightly with oil, and put it in a quart deli container with the lid on.
Refrigerate 3–5 days, which gives the lightest crust and the easiest rolling. Short on time? Overnight in the fridge still works, or ≈3 h at room temp until doubled.

Dust the counter generously with semolina. Roll one ball very thin into a 14 in circle, lifting and turning it as you go, and measure it. It can come straight from the fridge, though 1 h covered at room temp rolls easier. If it springs back, cover it with an upside-down bowl for 30 min and roll again. Repeat with the second ball.

Move each round onto its own sheet of parchment on a flat surface; the 3 × 2 ft cutting board fits both. Leave uncovered at room temp overnight, until the top is dry and leathery, like a flour tortilla. Push any bubbles flat with a fork.

nutritionSource: USDA FoodData Central: SR Legacy (sugar, canola oil, active dry yeast) and Branded Foods labels (King Arthur Unbleached Bread Flour, Morton). Water, semolina and the oil coating the balls not counted.
notes: The overnight cure is what makes the crust cracker-crisp, and it makes the round easy to top and move. Bake it the next day on the Chicago Tavern-Style Pizza card.
For 2 × 12 in crusts: 225 g flour, 5 g sugar, 5 g salt, 1 g yeast, 115 g water, 22.5 g oil.
No mixer? Food processor: run everything until the dough rides around the blade, then 30 s more. By hand: stir, rest 10 min, knead 7–10 min.
Baker’s %: flour 100, water 50, salt 2.3, sugar 2.3, oil 10, instant yeast 0.33.
